sources.title: Why We Should Build Software Like We Build Houses

verified_sections.section_or_page: p. 1: specification as a blueprint for thinking
p. 3: limits and continued need for coding-bug checks
2015 item and relation to prior 2013 article

verified_claims: Writing a specification supports thinking about intended behavior before coding.
The author treats formal specification as one end of a spectrum and normally uses informal specifications.
The author explicitly says writing specs alone does not ensure programs never crash.
sources.reader_action: Record what a caller must know to use the interface, along with unresolved choices, before choosing document length.
sources.proposed_artifact: One-page caller-behavior contract with failure meaning, compatibility promises, allowed freedom and open questions.
limits: Engineering argument and personal anecdotes; not causal effectiveness evidence.
Do not attribute 2015 expansion content to the 2013 copy.
No author anecdote timing is used as a numerical benefit claim.

sources.title: Introducing Example Mapping

verified_sections.section_or_page: So when do we write Gherkin?

verified_claims: Separates story, rules, concrete examples and unanswered questions.
Treats unclear expected outcomes as questions rather than settled examples.
Distinguishes discovering shared understanding from later formulation in Gherkin.
sources.reader_action: Bring unresolved policy to the responsible product/developer/tester participants instead of letting a generated test silently decide it.
sources.proposed_artifact: Rule/example/question/decision-owner table; suggested adaptation, not an existing author tool.
limits: The suggested meeting time is practitioner guidance, not an experimental optimum.
Existing formal study already fixed R01-R13; it did not evaluate this discovery process.

sources.title: BCP 14 requirement-level wording: RFC 2119 and RFC 8174

verified_sections.section_or_page: §6 do not impose implementation methods unnecessarily
§2 normative text need not use these keywords

verified_claims: Requirement strength differs from recommendation and option.
RFC 2119 §6 warns against imposing methods not required for interoperability.
RFC 8174 does not imply non-keyword text is non-normative.
sources.reader_action: Audit whether a wording edit changes the set of acceptable behaviors, and distinguish optional implementation hints from requirements.
sources.proposed_artifact: Allowed/forbidden/optional table, including both an invalid implementation and a different valid implementation.
limits: IETF scope; do not claim all repository documents must use BCP 14.
Do not pretend frozen A0-C explicitly adopted this uppercase convention.

sources.title: Hypothesis: Quickstart; Domain and distribution

verified_sections.section_or_page: How should I choose a domain for my test?
Okay, but what is the distribution?

verified_claims: Users select input domain; generation distribution is selected by Hypothesis.
Overly narrow domains can exclude bug-triggering values.
Generated inputs are not intended as uniform or production-realistic samples.
sources.reader_action: Review the property and the generator together; verify that null/falsy/type-boundary cases have not been filtered out.
limits: Passing generated inputs does not estimate production reliability.
This documentation does not establish the existing 103-check study used Hypothesis.
Do not use default example count as an assurance threshold.

sources.title: Metamorphic Testing: A New Approach for Generating Next Test Cases
sources.version: Technical Report HKUST-CS98-01; original PDF linked by coauthor

caches.method: gstack browse download then local pdftotext -layout

verified_sections.section_or_page: §2 p. 3: follow-up construction and practical constraints
§4 pp. 10-11: illustrative nature and incomplete methodology
coauthor publication list: title and original report identification

verified_claims: Previously successful cases can support new follow-up cases designed to reveal missed errors.
Domain knowledge is required to design meaningful follow-up relations.
The approach supplements other testing strategies; the report is primarily motivation and examples.
sources.reader_action: State source input, transformation, preconditions and output relationship before implementing a relation test.
sources.proposed_artifact: Blank-line insertion relation with diagnostic-line-number adjustment; duplication counterexample under R13.
limits: Worked parser examples are deductions from frozen requirements, not executed additions to the formal study.
The original PDF's extracted mathematical symbols contain OCR/encoding artifacts; do not quote formulas from text cache.
No large-scale experimental effectiveness claim is taken from this report.

sources.title: PIT: Basic Concepts
verified_claims: Mutations introduce changes whose effects a test may detect.
Equivalent or out-of-scope differences can legitimately survive.
PIT distinguishes survival, no coverage, invalid mutation and execution failures.
sources.reader_action: Classify surviving changes before adding assertions; pair negative controls with legal alternate implementations.
sources.proposed_artifact: Requirement-linked controlled-fault matrix with expected reject/accept disposition.
limits: PIT mutates Java bytecode; the study parser is Python.
Do not describe proposed targeted faults as executed results or claim a mutation score.
Mutation score alone is not a measure of complete specification correctness.

sources.title: Best practices for Claude Code

verified_sections.section_or_page: Give Claude a way to verify its work
Explore first, then plan, then code

verified_claims: Separates exploration/planning from implementation and gives an interview-to-spec pattern for larger features.
Recommends observable verification signals and fresh-context review.
Warns that excessive persistent instructions add noise and review prompts may induce unnecessary findings.
sources.reader_action: Separate project instructions, feature contract, executable checks and review criteria, then retain actual evidence.
sources.proposed_artifact: Versioned handoff record with scope, verification commands/results, unknowns and finding dispositions.
limits: Vendor practical guidance, not a randomized causal study.
Tool-enabled iterative workflows differ from the frozen tool-free one-shot study.
Fresh context does not establish independence of models or training data.
Do not repeat vendor promises of unattended correctness as a guarantee.

sources.title: Bidirectional Empowerment of Metamorphic Testing and Large Language Models: A Systematic Survey
sources.kind: research-author methodological synthesis; preprint survey, not a primary experiment
verified_claims: Plausible-sounding generated relations can be invalid or overly strong.
Paraphrases can legitimately change task meaning or expected responses.
One-shot relation violations in stochastic systems may mix defects and ordinary variability.
sources.reader_action: Require preconditions and a possible counterexample for a generated relation before treating it as a requirement.
sources.proposed_artifact: Relation-assurance card reviewed by the domain owner.
limits: Uses the authors' own methodological discussion, not reported effect sizes from cited third-party experiments.
HTML contains a placeholder DOI; do not claim formal CSUR publication.
Suggested assurance approaches are research directions, not proven guarantees.
The review's study count is unnecessary to the manuscript and is not used as an effectiveness denominator.
